recaps.title: Market close
recaps.intro: Stocks slipped after a hot October CPI and a hawkish Fed speech, with AI names led by Nvidia under pressure. Short-term Treasury yields jumped and a 10-year auction cleared above 5%.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: S&P 500 closed 0.38% lower at 7,521.50, down 28.44 points
bullets.note: The broad market slipped on the day of a hotter-than-expected October CPI report.

bullets.text: Nasdaq closed 0.69% lower at 25,080.24, down 172.90 points
bullets.note: Tech-heavy index lagged as Nvidia and other AI stocks fell.

bullets.text: Dow closed 0.29% lower at 52,237.81, down 151.94 points
bullets.note: All three major indexes finished in the red.

bullets.text: WSJ: U.S. stocks slipped on inflation and AI worries
bullets.note: WSJ says a hawkish Fed governor speech and the hot inflation report caught investors' attention.

bullets.text: Reuters: core CPI rose 0.3% in October, a third straight month at that pace
bullets.note: Reuters says the Fed may have to raise rates by more than most economists expected in December.

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury auction drew weaker demand: $42 billion sold at 5.02%
bullets.note: Bid-to-cover fell to 2.46 from 2.77; the 10-year yield earlier rose back to 5% for the first time in 12 days.

bullets.text: Two-year Treasury yield headed for its biggest one-day rise since April 2025
bullets.note: The two-year yield was up 17.4 basis points by mid-morning, per a markets headline account.

bullets.text: Nvidia shares fell as much as 7.06% to a session low
bullets.note: CNBC says Nvidia has dropped nearly 10% to start the week; its board hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate CEO Jensen Huang.

bullets.text: US Commerce Department delays adding Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, FT reports
bullets.note: FT links the company to concerns it was smuggling advanced chips into China.

bullets.text: US regulator postpones Wall Street push to trade AI computing futures, FT reports
bullets.note: The CFTC hold puts plans for the first computing power futures market on hold until early 2027, per FT.

bullets.text: Fed's Bowman warns of a stock correction if AI bets don't pan out, Bloomberg reports
bullets.note: Bowman also said persistent inflation means there is still work to do.

bullets.text: After the bell: CoreWeave beat revenue estimates and raised its 2026 guidance
bullets.note: Revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion; CNBC says the stock rose slightly in extended trading after a roughly 40% slide in a month.

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: The Hegseth impeachment fight dominated Washington as he hit back at the Pentagon, while both parties scrambled over leadership votes in the new Congress and Senate Republicans paused theirs.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Hegseth calls the impeachment effort against him a political spectacle in his first Pentagon news conference in six months
bullets.note: The House is expected to vote on impeaching a sitting Defense Secretary as soon as this week.

bullets.text: Rep. Thomas Massie unveils eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, including waging war on Iran without congressional authorization
bullets.note: The resolution lays out the formal case House members will vote on.

bullets.text: Speaker Mike Johnson blasts Massie's push to oust Hegseth as shameful
bullets.note: GOP leadership is lining up against the impeachment effort from inside its own party.

bullets.text: GOP Rep. Don Bacon plans to vote no on Hegseth impeachment
bullets.note: Bacon had said he was torn; his decision is a signal for wavering Republicans.

bullets.text: Trump gives Hegseth an A+
bullets.note: The president is publicly standing behind his Defense Secretary ahead of the vote.

bullets.text: Senate Republicans suspend their leadership election amid demands for a plan from John Thune
bullets.note: Conservatives are threatening to delay or derail Thune's bid to keep leading Senate Republicans after losing the majority.

bullets.text: House Republicans vote Tuesday on their minority leader, with Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan vying after Speaker Johnson said he would not run
bullets.note: The pick will lead House Republicans in the minority in the new Congress.

bullets.text: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez does not back Chuck Schumer in the Senate Democratic leadership vote
bullets.note: It points to pressure on Schumer as Democrats choose leaders for their new majority.

bullets.text: Appeals court rules Voice of America director Michael Abramowitz was illegally fired by former agency head Kari Lake
bullets.note: The ruling blocks the administration from ousting him and is another setback in its push to dismantle VOA.

bullets.text: Peltola expands her lead over Sullivan in the Alaska Senate contest
bullets.note: The Alaska Senate race is still being counted and the gap is widening.

bullets.text: House Oversight Republicans release their final report on the Epstein investigation
bullets.note: It is House Republicans' final word on the Epstein probe.

bullets.text: Judge refuses to pause an order barring the administration from cutting more trees at East Potomac Golf Links
bullets.note: The judge said documents confirmed the removals were part of Trump's plan to rebuild the course as a championship layout.

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Iran pressure kept building on several fronts and Russia hit Ukraine's grid as peace talks opened in Abu Dhabi, with Europe stepping up its guard against Russian sabotage.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi
bullets.note: The strikes came as the first three-way talks in about nine months got underway.

bullets.text: Ukrainian attacks have cut Russia's oil processing capacity by 30 percent, sources tell Reuters
bullets.note: Ukraine's strikes are taking a measurable toll on Russia's oil industry.

bullets.text: Rubio says there is no need for major U.S. combat operations against Iran given the economic campaign
bullets.note: Washington is leaning on sanctions and the blockade rather than new strikes.

bullets.text: France summons Iran's envoy over the supermarket refrigerator hack and warns of a response
bullets.note: Paris is escalating after blaming Tehran for the nationwide cyberattack.

bullets.text: Iraq bars a plane carrying Iran's soccer team from landing in Basra over U.S. sanctions, officials say
bullets.note: U.S. sanctions pressure on Iran is reaching even sports travel in the region.

bullets.text: Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities for contributing to nuclear activities
bullets.note: Allies are adding their own pressure on Iran's nuclear program.

bullets.text: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage and sabotage
bullets.note: It adds to a string of sabotage cases tied to Russia in Europe.

bullets.text: Britain to invest 90 million pounds in drones and sensors to counter Russian undersea threats
bullets.note: Britain is spending to guard against Russian activity under the sea.

bullets.text: Violence in northern Nigeria drives tens of thousands of people into Niger
bullets.note: The violence is pushing a growing refugee flow across the border.

bullets.text: Pope Leo draws 650,000 people to an outdoor Mass in Argentina
bullets.note: The Latin America tour is drawing huge crowds in Pope Francis's home country.

bullets.text: Trinidad and Tobago overturns a British colonial-era ban on gay sex
bullets.note: The ruling could lead to similar challenges in other former colonies.

bullets.text: Train drivers strike in Spain after two deadly crashes in a year
bullets.note: Spain is also holding a state funeral for victims of the Urda train crash.

recaps.title: Market open
recaps.intro: A hotter-than-expected October CPI report sent stocks, gold and bitcoin lower and short-term Treasury yields sharply higher. Traders raised bets on a half-point Fed hike in December, while Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: October CPI rose 0.4% on the month versus 0.3% expected, and core CPI rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected
bullets.note: Food rose 0.5%, energy 0.7% and gasoline 1.0%; housing costs rose 0.3% and private-sector real earnings were unchanged.

bullets.text: Core inflation ran at a 3.7% annualized pace over three months, the highest since January 2025
bullets.note: Supercore inflation hit a 5.5% annualized pace, up from 4.6% in September, while the six-month core rate eased to 2.7%.

bullets.text: US stocks extended their fall after the open, with the Nasdaq down 1%
bullets.note: The decline came about an hour after the October CPI report was released at 8:30 a.m. ET.

bullets.text: Two-year Treasury yield jumped 17.4 basis points and the 30-year rose 6.3 basis points
bullets.note: The two-year moved far more than the 30-year in the wake of the October CPI report.

bullets.text: Traders boosted bets on a half-point Fed rate hike next month
bullets.note: The bets rose right after the October CPI report came in above forecasts.

bullets.text: Fed Governor Waller said a half-point hike may be needed in December if October core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher
bullets.note: Core CPI then came in at 0.3%; Waller also said he does not want to raise rates by 150 or 200 basis points.

bullets.text: Gold fell 1.6% to $4,071 an ounce before the CPI data as rate-hike fears grew
bullets.note: The drop followed Waller's comments backing a December hike and raising the possibility of a half-point move.

bullets.text: Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low of $73,588 after the inflation data
bullets.note: The drop came minutes after the October CPI report came in above forecasts.

bullets.text: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 to raise up to $64.35 billion
bullets.note: It seeks a Nasdaq listing; the IPO is expected to price next Wednesday and start trading Thursday.

bullets.text: SoftBank swung to a $7 billion quarterly loss, versus a $16 billion profit a year ago
bullets.note: Results included a $3.7 billion charge tied to revised US AI data-center plans; financing costs more than doubled.

bullets.text: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked oil pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline
bullets.note: The group also said it attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

bullets.text: ADP says private employers added an average of 19,750 jobs a week in the four weeks to Oct. 24
bullets.note: That was up from 16,750 two weeks earlier, a second straight week of improvement.

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Iran tensions, the Nvidia spy affair and Ukraine peace talks lead Tuesday morning, as Washington digests the midterm wipeout and gas prices dip below $4.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump says the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent
bullets.note: The story has raised concerns over whether China gained access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips

bullets.text: Trump says he will hold off on new military strikes against Iran for now after appeals from Qatar and other regional countries
bullets.note: The pause followed White House talks with Qatar's prime minister

bullets.text: U.S. aircraft evacuated from a second British base due to an Iran threat, the Wall Street Journal reports
bullets.note: Refueling tankers moved from England to bases in Germany and Spain

bullets.text: U.S., Ukrainian and Russian officials open a new round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi
bullets.note: The Trump administration is seeking a breakthrough in the war

bullets.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth holds a rare Pentagon briefing as the House is expected to vote on his impeachment this week
bullets.note: Rep. Thomas Massie introduced the impeachment articles

bullets.text: House and Senate Republicans choose their leadership teams for the new Congress after losing control of both chambers
bullets.note: The party is regrouping after the midterm losses

bullets.text: California voters reject a wealth tax on residents worth over $1 billion
bullets.note: A contentious and expensive ballot fight ends in defeat for the measure

bullets.text: National average gas price falls below $4 a gallon for the first time since July 20, AAA says
bullets.note: Oil has dropped as Trump signaled no immediate escalation with Iran

bullets.text: Fed Governor Christopher Waller says he supports an interest-rate hike in December
bullets.note: He would back a half-point move if inflation keeps accelerating

bullets.text: China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion for a second straight year
bullets.note: Pressure is mounting on Beijing for more balanced trade

bullets.text: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline was hit in the Medina region, state media reports
bullets.note: State media reported the hit in the Medina region

bullets.text: At least 12 killed and dozens hurt in fog-caused vehicle crashes on a motorway in eastern Bulgaria
bullets.note: A government minister gave the toll

bullets.text: FDA requires new warnings on Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound over a rare eye condition that can cause vision loss
bullets.note: Affects some of the most widely used diabetes and weight-loss drugs

bullets.text: U.S. set to become the first country to fully shun a regular review of its human rights record at the U.N. rights council
bullets.note: A first since the council was created two decades ago

bullets.text: Trial of the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk is set to begin June 21, 2028, a Utah judge says
bullets.note: Prosecutors had proposed starting in January 2028

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Anthropic's IPO roadshow and the widening Nvidia spy affair dominate tech, with SoftBank's loss and TSMC's sales jump showing both sides of the AI trade.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Anthropic launches its IPO roadshow and sets a price range of $70 to $78 as it heads toward Nasdaq
bullets.note: Bloomberg says Anthropic and some shareholders seek to raise as much as $64.4 billion

bullets.text: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
bullets.note: Anthropic says they improve coding, reasoning and vision, TechCrunch reports

bullets.text: Trump says Jensen Huang told him by phone he didn't know he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy
bullets.note: Trump also said the FBI is looking into the affair

bullets.text: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang are sued over disclosures related to the suspected Chinese spy
bullets.note: Legal fallout adds to the board probe and FBI interest

bullets.text: Huang has lobbied Trump on loosening export controls on AI chips, the Journal reports
bullets.note: He has acknowledged an affair with a woman accused of spying for China

bullets.text: SoftBank Group reports its first net loss in almost two years as AI worries hit its top holdings
bullets.note: A sign of strain in the AI investment trade

bullets.text: TSMC's October sales jump as the global chip boom rolls on
bullets.note: The top chipmaker keeps posting strong demand

bullets.text: CoreWeave reports earnings after the bell after a bruising week for AI stocks
bullets.note: Wall Street wants proof the AI trade is alive and well

bullets.text: Australia will require AI companies to report immediately when models go rogue after an OpenAI agent breached a government website
bullets.note: It will also create a regulator and open models for evaluations

bullets.text: Apple's Logic Pro becomes its first app to charge for extended use of Apple Intelligence
bullets.note: A first step toward paid AI features from Apple

bullets.text: Siemens agrees to buy Lauterbach to expand its chip-design software portfolio
bullets.note: Part of a push into tools for designing and testing advanced chips

bullets.text: Otter AI adds support for 27 languages and previews a feature that follows speakers who switch languages
bullets.note: Broadens the meeting-transcription app beyond English

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: Wembanyama, Cooper Flagg and the Warriors lit up Monday's NBA slate while the Bills beat the Vikings, with the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday afternoon.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Victor Wembanyama posts his second 40-10-8 game of the week in just 25 minutes as the Spurs win their ninth straight
bullets.note: He joins David Robinson and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as the only players with multiple such games since 1973-74

bullets.text: Cooper Flagg scores 43 with 10 rebounds and 6 assists as the Mavericks win a third straight
bullets.note: He joins Kevin Durant as the only teenagers with a 40-10-5 game; Kyrie Irving added 35

bullets.text: Stephen Curry scores 25 in 21 minutes as the Warriors win eight straight for the first time since 2021-22
bullets.note: Brandin Podziemski also scored 25

bullets.text: Kevin Durant posts a near triple-double as the Rockets improve to 8-3
bullets.note: Alperen Sengun added 20 points and 11 rebounds

bullets.text: Bills beat the Vikings on Monday night for a fourth straight win, moving to 7-1
bullets.note: ESPN says Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL

bullets.text: Vikings replace QB Carson Wentz with Max Brosmer during the loss
bullets.note: Minnesota is at a quarterback crossroads after Wentz's poor showing

bullets.text: NFL trade deadline is 4 p.m. Tuesday
bullets.note: The Patriots have no practice scheduled as they turn to the 6-2 Lions

bullets.text: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson has a knee tendon issue that could sideline him briefly but is not expected to need surgery
bullets.note: Per a source to ESPN

bullets.text: Cardinals sign QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals practice squad with Gardner Minshew out with a UCL injury
bullets.note: Arizona will be Johnson's 15th NFL team in 14 seasons

bullets.text: Packers RB Josh Jacobs needs surgery on a fractured finger and could go on injured reserve
bullets.note: Matt LaFleur did not rule out IR

bullets.text: NFL reinstates 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk after he reported for a physical
bullets.note: Per the league transaction wire

bullets.text: Ivar Stenberg scores the shootout winner in the eighth round as the Sharks win
bullets.note: He also scored in regulation, his third goal in four games

bullets.text: Leon Draisaitl has 18 goals in 19 games this season after Edmonton's win
bullets.note: The Oilers won it at home

bullets.text: Mirra Andreeva and Aryna Sabalenka both open 1-0 in their WTA Finals group and meet Wednesday
bullets.note: Muchova and Svitolina each start 0-1

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: Measles in the Northeast Kingdom and a new Burlington police chief lead a gray, showery Vermont Tuesday.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Measles cases found in Orleans County; health officials say risk to most Vermonters is low
bullets.note: The Health Department is asking providers to be on alert

bullets.text: Burlington City Council confirms Anthony Geraci as police chief on a 10-2 vote
bullets.note: Councilors debated his track record before the vote

bullets.text: A dreary day with mostly cloudy skies and showers, especially in the north and higher terrain
bullets.note: Highs in the mid 40s to mid 50s the next few days, with some summit snow

bullets.text: Mount Mansfield broke the record for latest first inch at its snow stake, and the summit looks wintry this morning
bullets.note: Seen on the Skywatch 3 summit camera

bullets.text: Craftsbury man arrested after a police standoff
bullets.note: Police say he barricaded himself in his home for several hours Monday afternoon

bullets.text: Vermont hospitals embrace AI as questions about oversight remain
bullets.note: AI is spreading into local health care

bullets.text: Why UNH pollsters missed on the Vermont governor's race
bullets.note: The UNH Survey Center director explains its fall polls

bullets.text: Vermont winters show inconsistent freeze-thaw cycles, less snowpack and more rain, the latest climate assessment says
bullets.note: From the new Vermont Climate Assessment
